question.text: This is the total number of women who have ever been Supreme Court justices, past and present.
question.clue: The Algerian War of Independence led to the collapse of the French republic of this number. The Knights Templar were disbanded under a French king of this regnal number nicknamed "The Fair."

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about dynasties of China.
swap.text: This last imperial dynasty of China was overthrown by the Xinhai ["sheen-hi"] Revolution. This dynasty fought the Opium Wars with Great Britain and the Sino-Japanese wars with Japan.
swap.clue: This dynasty's "century of humiliation" resulted after it was forced to sign a sequence of "unequal treaties'" marking its defeat in the Opium Wars.

question.leadin: The failed Hundred Days' Reform occurred during this event.
question.text: Name this uprising against foreigners by the Society of Righteous and Harmonious Fists which saw the Empress Dowager Cixi declare war on an eight nation alliance.
question.clue: This conflict was formally ordered by Empress Dowager Cixi ].

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Chinese history.
swap.text: This rebellion's leader, Hong Xiuquan, claimed to be the brother of Jesus, and it attempted to establish a "Heavenly Kingdom" in mid-nineteenth century China.
swap.clue: The majority of those who participated belonged to the Hakka class, and soon after one of their armies was repulsed by Frederick Townsend Ward, their leader took poison and died in a sewer.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the history of medieval navies.
question.text: The naval history of the Ming Dynasty saw this man lead seven treasure voyages around the Indian Ocean. This Muslim captain defeated the pirate Chen Zuyi and brought exotic animals from Africa to the Chinese court.
question.clue: A controversial 2002 work by Gavin Menzies claimed that this man discovered the Americas, Australia, and the Northeast Passage.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the People's Republic of China.
swap.text: During the Chinese Revolution, Mao was opposed by this political party, which was headed by Chiang Kai-shek; most of its members eventually fled to Taiwan.
swap.clue: One leader of this party adapted Henry George's philosophy to form his Three Principles of the People.

question.leadin: This dynasty's Southern period began after its emperor was captured and its capital, Kaifeng, sacked by invading Jurchens.
question.text: Name this dynasty, which followed the Tang Dynasty and was supplanted by Kublai Khan's Yuan Dynasty. This dynasty was the first to use gunpowder.
question.clue: Bi Sheng worked under this dynasty, which switched lines of succession due to the Jingkang Incident.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about famous bridges in Chinese history.
swap.text: During this event, Edgar Snow recounts how soldiers bravely crossed the Luding chain bridge under machine gun fire and defeated their opponents. This event took place following the Fifth Encirclement Campaign.
swap.clue: The Fifth Encirclement forced this event, which Otto Braun took part in. The participants of this event defeated warlord forces at the Battle of Luding Bridge and reshuffled their leadership at the Zunyi Conference.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about abductions in Chinese history.
question.text: Manchurian Marshal Zhang Xueliang nabbed this leader of the Kuomintang in the Xi'an Incident and held him hostage until his Nationalist forces reached an agreement with Mao's Communist forces to resist the Japanese.
question.clue: The February 28 incident was also put down by this leader, who was the first commandant of the Whampoa Military Academy.

swap.leadin: This dynasty defeated its predecessor at the Battle of Muye, capturing its capital at modern Anyang.
swap.text: Name this longest ruling Chinese dynasty who thereafter became the first to claim a "Mandate of Heaven" for their rule.
swap.clue: The Hundred Schools flourished during the Eastern part of the dynasty, whose rulers were the first to claim the (* ) Mandate of Heaven.

question.leadin: The yin privilege allowed high ranking bureaucrats to place their sons into low positions of power without having to deal with this system.
question.text: Name this system, success in which allowed scholar-bureaucrats to advance by demonstrating knowledge of wenxue. The challenging Eight-legged essay was an integral part of this system.
question.answerHtml: Chinese imperial examinations [accept equivalents like the Chinese civil service exams]

swap.leadin: This scholar was forced to choose between execution and castration for defending Li Ling after Li was captured by the Xiongnu ("sh'yung-noo").
swap.text: Name this thinker who accepted castration in order to finish his magnum opus, Records of the Grand Historian, which covers 2500 years of Chinese history.
swap.clue: This court eunuch wrote a biography of emperors starting with Huangdi, also known as the Yellow Emperor, to his contemporary Emperor Wu of Han.

question.text: The Baltic countries gained independence from the Soviet Union in a "revolution" named for this action. That revolution named for this action included the formation of a human chain across all three countries.
question.answerHtml: singing [accept Singing Revolution or laulev revolutsioon or dziesmotā revolūcija or dainuojanti revoliucija]
question.clue: The Tibeto-Burman Lisu people pass on their history through works in this art form which may take a whole night to perform. The all-women group Tyva Kyzy popularized a variety of this musical performance called Khoomei native to and often named for the country of Tuva.

swap.leadin: The Cheng Wu manuscript describes a dream of this dynasty's queen Tai Si foretelling their victory over their predecessors.
swap.text: Name this dynasty established after its predecessors were defeated at the Battle of Muye. The Five Classics, including the I Ching, are traditionally thought to have been written during this dynasty.
swap.answerHtml: Zhōu (“joe”) dynasty [or Zhōu Cháo; accept Eastern Zhōu or Western Zhōu or Xīzhōu or Dōngzhōu]
swap.clue: Wu was also the son of King Weng, who is credited with being this dynasty's first emperor.

question.leadin: This movement began with a speech called "On the Correct Handling of the Contradictions Among the People."
question.text: Name this 1956 movement in which citizens were briefly encouraged to express their true opinions about the Chinese government. It didn't last long.
question.clue: One element of this effort was an attempt to cooperate with the CUF and it was introduced in a speech entitled, "On the Correct Handling of Contradictions Among the People."

swap.leadin: The "peach-plum prophecy," which cryptically suggested that someone with this family name would overthrow the Sui, was fulfilled by Gaozu's founding of the Tang dynasty.
swap.text: Give this family name. Much later, having this auspicious family name helped a "dashing prince" to assemble a rebel army that overthrew the Ming dynasty and installed him as emperor of the short-lived Shun dynasty.
swap.clue: A powerful governor of the Longxi Commandery from this family used Gokturk support to install the puppet emperor Yang You before toppling him and establishing a ruling dynasty.

question.leadin: The Mongol invasion of China subjugated this northern kingdom whose own invasion of China had led to the formation of the Southern Song.
question.text: Name this dynasty founded by the Jurchens, whose name literally means "gold" in Chinese.
question.clue: The next masters of the northern Chinese frontier were this dynasty, which overthrew the Liao and ruled from 1115 to 1234, when their capital of Kaifeng fell. They banned all Chinese culture from their army in an attempt to preserve their ethnic identity.

swap.leadin: During its Eastern phase, this dynasty granted tax exemptions to resettled migrants from north China called qiaoren.
swap.text: Name this dynasty ruled by the Sima family, whose earlier Western phase began with its reunification of China in 280 CE and ended following multiple civil wars named for Eight Princes and Five Barbarians.
swap.clue: Its forces expelled the ruler Yelu Dashi to the west, where he founded the Kara-Khitan Khanate with surviving forces of the Liao dynasty.

question.leadin: A ruler of this dynasty had a concubine who requested a lake of alcohol and then had 3,000 men drink it dry; of course, they drowned.
question.text: What dynasty's troops, under the command of the corrupt Jie, lost to the forces of a man named Tang at the battle of Mingtiao?
question.clue: A concubine of a ruler of this dynasty supposedly filled a lake with wine and ordered 3,000 men to drink it dry.

swap.text: This Chinese monk recounted Harsha's defeat at the Narmada River as part of the Great Tang Records on the Western Regions that he wrote in his 17 years of travelling through India, which were inspired by Faxian.
swap.clue: The Monkey King must defend this monk from demons who want to gain immortality by eating him. While conducting the ceremony of Shui Lu Da Hui, this man is told to make a pilgrimage to the Western Heaven.
